item.title: Jetten and Burnham pledge to keep up support for Ukraine
item.description:
Jetten and Burnham pledge to keep up support for Ukraine

November 23, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten and his British counterpart Andy Burnham have pledged to keep up support for Ukraine as Burnham made his first official visit to the Netherlands since taking office in July.

The two leaders also discussed last week’s summit between the UK and the European Union in Brussels as Burnham tries to rebuild relations with continental Europe after Brexit.

In a post on social media site X, Jetten said he valued the “long and close” relationship between the two countries as “neighbours, allies and partners in Europe”.

“Our countries have worked together for years for a stronger and safer Europe,” Jetten said. “It is a pleasure to build on that co-operation together with Andy Burnham”.

Burnham said he and Jetten “agreed on the vital need to keep the pressure up on Russia to bring Putin to the negotiations table” and the two countries would continue to support Ukraine in order to “secure a lasting, durable peace”.

In a statement on the UK government website, he also thanked the Dutch prime minister for his support in securing what he called “a win-win deal for Britain and the EU.”

As part of the deal agreed in Brussels, the two sides agreed to scrap most border checks on agricultural exports and allow up to 100,000 young people to move across the border to live and work for up to three years.

The Netherlands is the UK’s third largest trading partner, account for 6.3% of British trade. Dutch foreign direct investment in the UK makes up 9.4% of the total.

Jetten and Burnham had dinner in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam on Saturday evening, together with Jetten’s fiancé Nicolas Keenan and Burnham’s Dutch wife, Marie-France van Heel.

On Sunday the British prime minister was in Rotterdam, where he watched AZ beat Sparta 5-1, accompanied by mayor Carola Schouten.

item.title: Offline, on the floor and in the sauna
item.description:
Offline, on the floor and in the sauna

November 23, 2026 Molly Quell

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

While much of Amsterdam was enjoying a night out at a bar or restaurant on a Saturday evening, on a boat on the IJ, a group was listening to the dulcet tones of a clarinet while wrapped in bathrobes.

Stoom Goes Deeper is the brainchild of entrepreneur Sjoerd Schaap, whose latest venture is a sauna and hotel aboard a former paddle steamer docked at the NDSM wharf.

It’s “an evening of sound, breath and heat,” Schaap told Dutch News.

I received an invitation to attend the event after Schaap read my column about surviving a Dutch sauna experience, which I guess makes me Dutch News’ official Sauna Correspondent.

You can find Kapitein Anna at the end of the pier, just past the Botel. The ship, built in 1911, now has 14 hotel rooms and multiple saunas. If you’ve ever taken the ferry to Amsterdam Noord and wondered why there are a lot of people lounging around in swimwear, you’re looking into Stoom’s main sauna.

The stern of the boat has been turned entirely into a sauna with a view of Amsterdam Centraal and the Pontsteiger.

Bucking Dutch tradition, swimwear is required. “We want everyone to feel included,” Schaap said.

Stoom Goes Deeper was in its second edition when I attended.

Around 40 people from a variety of ages and nationalities spread out on yoga mats or on the lounge seating on Kapitein Anna’s main deck. Most wore bathrobes and sweatpants. They tucked themselves into towels and blankets.

The evening was emceed by Joep Mencke, a DJ and “breathwork facilitator.” For about 90 minutes, Mencke played relaxing tunes, accompanied by a clarinetist, and instructed the group through a series of breathing exercises.

Afterwards, everyone went into the sauna.

It’s “a moment to step away from the everyday and reconnect with yourself,” said Schaap.

I am not a person who is especially into meditation, and my engineer husband was skeptical of the “journey”, as Mencke described it, but lying around, with no phone, listening to lovely music was a delightful way to spend a Saturday evening.

“Breathwork has really helped me, it helps me relax, it takes me to another place where I can process things,” Claire Hoekstra told Dutch News. She had come to the event with a friend.

Most of the attendees came in pairs – there were a lot of couples – or small groups. But several came by themselves. Schaap bills the event as a “social sauna” and several people introduce themselves to one another. Two men were even exchanging business cards as they were leaving.

There is a bar as well, including lots of hydrating and electrolyte-filled options for anyone sweating it out.

The highlight for me was the sauna. The view onto the IJ at night is gorgeous and there’s a real thrill of sitting in a sauna, watching the ferries dock and depart.

Schaap intends to continue the events after the success of the first two. But if Stoom Goes Deeper doesn’t sound up your alley, the sauna facilities are open during the day as well.

I stayed in the hotel for the evening rather than ruining my relaxation on a night train. Standing outside in the fresh air on the ferry ride back to the station, I watched the Kapitein Anna as we passed. The sauna wasn’t yet open.

Maybe the next event should be Stoom Goes Earlier.

item.title: Dutch influencer freed from US after 11 days in ICE detention
item.description:
Dutch influencer freed from US after 11 days in ICE detention

November 23, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A Dutch social media influencer and model who was arrested in the US by the immigration security service ICE has been returned to the Netherlands after 11 days in a notorious detention facility in Newark.

Vera Dijkmans, who has millions of online followers and has been doing promotional work for the US cage fighting organisation UFC, was taken by ICE agents after apparently failing to comply with her visa conditions.

Her mother, who has been publicly protesting her daughter’s detention, told Omroep Brabant that the experience had left Vera “severely weakened”. The Delaney Hall immigration detention facility, which houses around 1,000, has been noted for its grueling conditions.

The Dijkmans family was not given any official reason for Vera’s detention. Once her mother had traveled to the US to press for her release, her daughter told her of the lack of food, fresh air and cramped conditions.

Conditions in the facility, which was reopened and expanded by the Trump administration, led to a hunger strike by detainees in 2016. It is run by private prison company GEO Group, which was awarded a 15-year, $1 billion contract by ICE in 2025

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry told the press that it was aware of Dijkmans’ incarceration, and said it was providing consular assistance. The US government issued a warning this year about making financial gains in the country through social media while on tourist visas.

item.title: Regional transport strikes begin: where services are hit
item.description:
Regional transport strikes begin: where services are hit

November 23, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Regional transport workers have started a two-day strike on Monday morning in protest to working conditions, negotiations over which failed last week.

The strikes will hit local bus and train services throughout the country today and on Tuesday. If this doesn’t persuade employees to heed workers’ demands, the unions say further strikes are already planned for December 3, 4, 14, 15 and 18.

Around 13,000 transport workers are covered by agreements with employees’ association VWOV, and are demanding better pay and working conditions. Staff at Arriva, Transdev, EBS, Qbuzz, Keolis and RET’s are joining the strikes.

According to workers’ unions FNV and CNV, they object to plans to scrap the average allowance for working irregular hours, to raise the age at which older drivers are spared late shifts from 50 to 53, and to restrict a scheme that allows staff over 63 to work less.

In Rotterdam, RET buses are not running at all, and in Utrecht trams 20 and 22 and around 30 city bus routes are suspended. North Brabant is among the worst-hit areas, with only 10% to 15% of Arriva buses operating, and there are no Arriva trains between Nijmegen and Roermond.

Keolis is running fewer trains in the east and fewer buses in Almere and the Utrecht region, while Qbuzz and EBS expect reduced services in parts of South Holland, Friesland, Groningen, Drenthe and Zaanstreek-Waterland. Services are largely unaffected in the Achterhoek, on Arriva’s northern rail lines and in Amsterdam and The Hague, and NS trains are running normally.

item.title: Ajax go second in Eredivisie behind PSV as Feyenoord woes deepen
item.description:
Ajax go second in Eredivisie behind PSV as Feyenoord woes deepen

November 23, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV stay top

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

item.title: Sunny but cold week ahead with sub-zero nights
item.description:
Sunny but cold week ahead with sub-zero nights

November 23, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Monday will be mostly sunny and dry after a night’s frost, with temperatures rising to between 4° in the southeast and 8° on the northwest coast, according to the national weather service KNMI.

Temperatures fell to around -6° in the east and southeast overnight. Mist could linger in the southeast and southern Limburg will stay cloudy, while cloud coming in from the North Sea could cover parts of the north. KNMI has not issued any weather warnings for Monday, after code yellow alerts for fog and slippery roads on Sunday morning.

Tonight will be cold again, with lows of around -4° inland and 2° on the coast. Weather bureau Weeronline says temperatures could drop to -5° in some places overnight into Tuesday, which counts as moderate frost.

The rest of the week will stay dry and largely sunny but get colder. KNMI forecasts a high of 3° on Tuesday, falling to 1° or 2° from Wednesday to Friday, with frost every night. Weeronline and Weerplaza both say an easterly wind will pick up from Wednesday, so it will feel below freezing even during the day.

Weeronline says mist may hang around for a long time on some mornings. It will not yet be cold enough for skating on natural ice on a large scale, it says, though some natural ice rinks may open after a cold night.

item.title: IDFA 2026 winners: Chinese family portrait takes top prize
item.description:
IDFA 2026 winners: Chinese family portrait takes top prize

November 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Year of the Ghost, a Dutch-Chinese documentary about a filmmaker’s mother and sister after his father’s death, has won the top prize at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

Louis Hothothot’s film won three awards at Thursday’s ceremony at the Eye Filmmuseum. It took best film in the International Competition, which carries a €15,000 prize, as well as best editing and the €5,000 award for best Dutch film.

The festival’s 39th edition runs until Sunday, with 253 films from 80 countries. One of the five documentaries in our preview, You Can See Everything, came second in the audience vote.

These are the films that took the main prizes:

The Year of the Ghost
Hothothot was born in China in 1986 as a second child under the one-child policy and moved to Amsterdam in his twenties. His first film, Four Journeys, opened at IDFA in 2021. In this second film, Covid restrictions stop him from getting back to China in time to say goodbye to his father. He then follows his mother, who wants to stay in her husband’s home town to care for his spirit, and his sister, who is trying to get by as a single woman in a big city. The jury praised the film’s “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love”.

Memories of Lightning
Riccardo Giacconi’s French-Italian film won best film in the Envision Competition for experimental work, also worth €15,000. Radio journalist Sibilla Scinti Roger (30) travels to an almost deserted village in Le Marche, central Italy, to make an audio documentary about a murder there in 1982 – and finds out the 14-year-old victim was her aunt. Scinti Roger also won the award for outstanding artistic contribution.

Hazara Town
Afghan-born director Khadim Dai won the award for best first feature and the international critics’ prize (Fipresci), as well as a special mention in the International Competition. The film follows his Hazara family, who fled Afghanistan 20 years ago and now face growing persecution in Pakistan. They have to decide whether to stay together or leave one by one, knowing they may never see each other again.

The Clearing
Dutch director Sabine Groenewegen won the award for best use of archive footage, sponsored by the media archive Beeld & Geluid. Her film is a feminist history of Dutch colonial rubber plantations in the Dutch East Indies, where local women were subjected to violence and sexual enslavement. On the festival’s opening night, Groenewegen also received the €50,000 Cultuurfonds documentary grant, which an anonymous donor gives every year to a Dutch documentary maker.

Women and War
The €5,000 audience award, announced on Friday, went to Elwira Niewiera’s German-Polish-Ukrainian documentary. Four women attend therapy sessions in a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, each trying to recover from very different traumatic experiences of the war. Festivalgoers gave it an average score of 4.856 out of 5, just ahead of You Can See Everything on 4.842.

Other winners included Joël Akafou’s Lonan Tché for best directing and Tala Hadid’s Bardi, set among horse riders in central Morocco, for best cinematography. Raluca Lupaşcu’s A Modern Roma Fairytale got a special mention for best Dutch film, and Ant Hampton’s Dutch-Belgian All the Downtime won the DocLab award for digital storytelling.

The full list of winners is on the IDFA website.

item.title: Inburgering with DN: understanding education system acronyms
item.description:
Inburgering with DN: understanding education system acronyms

November 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

International parents in the Netherlands often find the Dutch school system baffling: HBO, SBO, DUO, WO… the jargon is endless. So to help you pass this particular parenting test, our Inburgering course this month looks at educational acronyms and the like.

Lesson 65: educational jargon

Primary school in the Netherlands is relatively straightforward – although parents often face a bewildering number of school philosophies when deciding which school to entrust their offspring to. It is in groep 8, the final year of primary school, that the trouble really starts.

Doorstroomtoets
Previously known as the Citotoets and the Eindtoets Basisonderwijs, the doorstroomtoets is taken by children in their final year at primary school. The tests focus on language and arithmetic, and the results are used to help determine which type of secondary education children should go on to. In principle, the teacher’s recommendation takes precedence.

The Dutch love of tests and early streaming has been widely criticised, and more secondary schools now offer mixed-ability classes in the first and second years.

Secondary education itself is divided into three main streams. Schools may offer just one – typically in cities – or a combination.

VWO
VWO (voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs, or preparatory academic education) is the highest level of Dutch secondary education and is followed by some 20% of pupils. A VWO education takes six years, with pupils choosing a specialism (profiel) in the sciences or humanities after three. There are two variants: atheneum and gymnasium. Gymnasium pupils take Latin and Greek in addition to the dozen or so other VWO subjects.

HAVO
HAVO (hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs) literally means ‘higher general continued education’. It takes five years to get a HAVO diploma, which prepares school leavers for a hogeschool (see HBO below) rather than a university. Around 30% of pupils are in a HAVO stream. After three years, HAVO pupils also choose a specialism in the sciences or humanities.

VMBO
VMBO stands for voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (preparatory intermediate vocational education). Some 50% of pupils attend this type of secondary education, which is subdivided into four streams. It takes four years to complete a VMBO course.

The most academic VMBO stream is still widely known as MAVO (middelbaar algemeen voortgezet onderwijs, or intermediate general continued education), after the type of school it replaced in 1999.

Middle-class parents push hard to avoid a VMBO recommendation, hence the popularity of tutors and crammers – and exam stress – for 12-year-olds.

SBO, SO and VSO
Special needs pupils have their own category of jargon, depending on their age, the nature of their disability and how much care they need. The main types are speciaal basisonderwijs (SBO, special primary education), speciaal onderwijs (SO, special education) and voortgezet speciaal onderwijs (VSO, special secondary education).

Lighthouse Special Education in The Hague is the only international school for special needs pupils.

After secondary school, most young people move on to further education. Education is compulsory until 16, and until 18 for anyone who does not yet have at least a HAVO, VWO or MBO level 2 diploma.

MBO
MBO, or middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vocational education and training), is the highest level of education reached by around 40% of the working population. There are four levels of MBO diploma, and students can either attend college full time or combine work and study.

HBO
There are two types of degree course in the Netherlands: the academic courses offered by universities and the more vocational courses (HBO, or hoger beroepsonderwijs) offered by hogescholen. Their umbrella body, the Vereniging Hogescholen, calls them ‘universities of applied sciences’ in English. The Netherlands has 36 hogescholen ranging from art academies to hotel schools and technical colleges.

WO
The Netherlands has 14 official universities offering wetenschappelijk onderwijs (research-oriented education), including the Open University. Delft, Eindhoven and Twente are universities of technology, while Wageningen focuses on agriculture and food. A bachelor’s degree takes three years, a master’s one or two.

DUO
If you have any connection to post-school education, you cannot avoid dealing with the education ministry’s Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO), which runs student finance and related services. DUO holds the diploma records that colleges and universities use to check whether you can enrol, organises the lotteries for popular courses and works out how much student finance you are entitled to.

After you graduate, DUO will follow you for years to make sure you pay back your student loan. DUO should not be confused with DUWO, which specialises in student housing.

item.title: Prosecutors hacked and wiretapped Tata Steel, court hears
item.description:
Prosecutors hacked and wiretapped Tata Steel, court hears

November 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The public prosecution service (OM) hacked into Tata Steel’s internal communication network, wiretapped phones, and made video recordings as part of its investigation into alleged criminal pollution, it was revealed on Friday in Amsterdam’s district court.

During the first hearing of the case, the OM revealed it had conducted a “covert intrusion into Tata Steel’s corporate network”, broadcaster NOS reported. Documents were also taken, witnesses questioned and deposition measurements examined.

The case, which has been years in the making, accuses the steelmaker of intentionally ignoring harmful pollution stemming from its coke and gas plants in IJmuiden.

Police and prosecutors are allowed to use hacking techniques in criminal cases under highly specific circumstances. This has been allowed since 2019, NOS reported, and only in a handful of cases, including child pornography and criminal communication investigations.

A defence lawyer for Tata Steel said that there was “unfounded distrust” against the company, that its employees go to work to do the right thing, and that “wire tapping and hacking” had been used as part of an “unbalanced” criminal file.

The investigation is ongoing and could lead to the prosecution of individual executives of the company. The process is not expected to be completed until the first quarter of next year, the OM said, at which point it will also become clear if the current CEO Hans van den Berg could be charged.

The public health institute RIVM records an above-average rate of lung cancer for residents living around the plant, and soot regularly collects in the surrounding neighbourhoods, including school playgrounds.

Many people have suffered serious health problems, which they attribute to the plant.

In 2021, lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of 1,200 residents and the following year prosecutors began investigating. In July, the OM summoned Tata Steel to court on criminal charges.

Shortly thereafter, the government said it could pull out of a planned €2 billion subsidy package for the company if the criminal case raises “serious concerns” for the Dutch state.

Podcast: The You Had One Job, Rob Jetten Edition

November 20, 2026

Want to support the Dutch News podcast so we don’t have to sell our children at a far-right cage fight? Click here to become a Patreon backer

The coalition parties emerge from a weekend of crisis talks agreeing to ruin Sybrand Buma’s Christmas by asking him to chair reconciliation talks after last week’s budget debacle. To the shock of absolutely nobody, Forum voor Democratie turns out to be infested with neo-Nazis who spend their leisure hours cage fighting and celebrating Hitler’s birthday in the Luxembourg forest. The Netherlands continues to lag behind on disability access and women’s pay, despite making progress in both areas. Dutch weapons manufacturer Destinus claims the credit for destroying part of Vladimir Putin’s flagship bridge to Crimea. A Van Gogh painting that was at the centre of a Nazi-era ownership dispute fetches a record price at auction. And in sport, Oranje go down to one of their worst defeats to old rivals Germany just days after achieving an epic victory against Greece.
